$comment: What this extension builds from. A bump is a PR; docs/PACKAGING.md says how. opentide.version is the @opentide/opentide each platform VSIX carries (dist/opentide), and the opentide CI tests the extension against. The highlights zip and the engine come from one engine release.

opentide.$comment: The @opentide/opentide (the Rust core: SDK and opentide command line) each platform VSIX carries in dist/opentide, run as a process of its own. npm.integrity is each tarball's npm dist.integrity, filled once the version is on npm; until then nothing is fetched from the registry, and builds take the package from OPENTIDE_NPM (tarballs or a built bindings/node), which CI builds from source.ref.

source.$comment: Until @opentide/opentide is on npm: the opentide commit CI builds bindings/node from (integration/unified-core with feat/uc-6-2, opentidehq/opentide#1020). Drop it once npm.integrity is filled.

engine.$comment: The opentide language server built for WebAssembly (wasm-bindgen --target web): the lowest runtime tier, editor features with nothing installed, and the engine of the web extension. From the same language-server release as the highlights zip.

platform.$comment: A platform VSIX (npm run package -- --target <target>): the universal one plus @opentide/opentide's native addon in dist/opentide, about 17 MiB compressed (52 MB installed) for linux-x64 at 0.24.0.
